target_customer: VR headset owners who buy and play a paid then free to play online game; later game studios buying AI developer tools
problem: VR lacked a large persistent online world with deep progression, and later game developers needed faster ways to build gameplay, assets and levels.
business_model: Premium game sales, then free to play with in game purchases (Zennies currency); later B2B AI agent tools for game engines
product_category: VR MMO game studio, later AI tools for game development

founders.name: Andy Tsen
founders.background_notes: YC page describes his focus as product, engineering and game development. No education or employers in sources opened.

founders.name: Lauren Frazier
founders.background_notes: Named as CTO in TechCrunch, August 2019, and as co-founder with Andy Tsen in a podcast listing. No background found.

competitors.name: OrbusVR
competitors.what: Indie VR MMORPG for SteamVR headsets with open world, dungeons and co-op
competitors.traction_then: Early access launched December 2017; six person team at Ad Alternum

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a persistent online VR world on Improbable's SpatialOS with PC VR, PlayStation VR and Oculus Quest targets, per TechCrunch 2019, is hard for a tiny team: networking at scale, VR comfort and content production.

defensibility.rationale: A game can be copied and players leave; a social world could build network effects but retention data later showed most players stopped after about a month.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform owners funded VR content rather than copying it; Meta Oculus took part in funding the game. No incumbent bought the studio in sources found.

market_need_then: VR headset sales were growing with Oculus Quest launching in 2019 and few large persistent VR games existed; the Kickstarter raised about 280,000 dollars against a 25,000 dollar goal from thousands of backers, showing player demand.

branding.name_origin: Co-founder Andy Tsen jokes the studio name comes from all they could afford to eat at the time (per a search summary of a published interview; interview not opened).
branding.domain_note: Uses ramenvr.com; the site now presents the company as Ramen.

identity.visual_style: Anime inspired cyberpunk with 80s futuristic look for Zenith, per TechCrunch

branding.brand_signature: Zenith: The Last City, a #1 VR game on Steam and Quest

rebrands.why: Shift from VR game studio to AI tools; reason not stated in sources, date approximate

branding.community_and_virality: Zenith built a player community and a record Kickstarter for VR; hundreds of thousands of players are claimed in a search summary.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable ramen studio name and a hit VR title with a Kickstarter that overfunded, but the VR in the name no longer fits the AI tools pivot and brand reach stayed within VR gaming.

pivots.why: Zenith got a final content update and price cut as development stopped in August 2024; studio later cited financial losses and low player retention.

outcome_analysis: Ramen VR got a strong start with a Kickstarter that overfunded in 2019, then raised 10 million in Series A and 35 million in Series B in 2021 and 2022 and shipped Zenith as a hit VR title. Most players left after about a month and the game lost money, so development stopped in August 2024 and servers close in December 2026. The company is still active, now building AI agents for game engines, so the company survived the game's failure through a pivot whose results are not yet clear.
notes: Kickstarter amount 280,075 is from a search summary of coverage (TechCrunch reported 132,000 a week into the campaign); recorded as other since it is crowdfunding. YC page says over 40 million raised, consistent with the rounds. Series B press release carries a 2021 date that looks like a typo; other outlets say March 2022 and YC page says March 19, 2022. Series A reported by Road to VR on 2021-09-27 with a search summary saying earlier funding totaled 173,000 plus an Oculus funding partnership; not recorded as rounds. Exit is none because the company is active; only the Zenith game is shutting down (announced October 2026). Competitor list limited to one rival with a dated source; the TechCrunch launch post names none. Name origin is from an unopened interview quoted in search results.
